chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Bedouins do not shorten [their prayers], and that is because their houses are with them.
ai.seo_question: Why do Bedouins not shorten their prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the exemption from shortening prayers (Qasr) for Bedouins stems from their mobile lifestyle, where their 'houses' and livelihoods travel with them, distinguishing them from settled populations who leave fixed residences. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the definition of 'travel' (safar) is tied to the departure from one's established home base, a concept deeply rooted in the practical realities of 7th-century Arabian society. Scholars note that this specific reasoning underscores the flexibility of fiqh in accommodating different social structures while maintaining the spiritual discipline of prayer.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far Al Ja’fary, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Bedouins would not be shortening, and that is because their houses are with them (like the nomads and the gypsies etc.)’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from his father from Sulayman ibn Ja‘far al- Ja‘fariy from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Arabs (desert dwellers) do not perform their Salah (prayer) as reduced because their homes are with them.’”
